paras: The brown-rumped bunting (Fringillariaa affinis) is a species of bird in the family Emberizidae native to the Sudan (region) and adjacent areas. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests.
This species was formerly placed in the genus Emberiza. In 2026 it was moved to the resurrected genus Fringillaria based on the results of a 2021 molecular genetic study.
F. a. nigeriae (Bannerman & Bates, 1926) – Gambia to Nigeria and northern Cameroon
F. a. vulpecula (Grote, 1921) – Cameroon, southern Chad, and adjacent northern Central African Republic

F. a. affinis (Heuglin, 1867) – South Sudan, northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, northern Uganda and northwestern Kenya; population in southeastern Sudan and northwestern Ethiopia presumably also this subspecies
